prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: new scenery illustration for the Split beer game, opaque full-bleed 1024 x 1536 portrait.
Input image: Image 1 is ONLY a style and composition reference, not an edit target. Make a NEW distinct place and scene. Match its rich painted gouache and colored-pencil travel-postcard brushwork, believable depth, tactile worn surfaces and warm human scale. Do not copy its pub/cantina architecture, beer bottles, signage, religious skyline details or existing setting.
Composition: a broad EMPTY foreground tabletop occupies approximately the bottom 40% of the portrait, with its rear edge around y=60%. Its center x=30–70% must be entirely unobstructed bare wood, reserved for a separately rendered live beer vessel. Every person, ritual object, lamp, pastry or game piece is on a side/background surface behind that rear edge, well away from the central live-vessel zone.
Scene: a quiet, welcoming Jewish city apartment at blue winter dusk, with a muted city skyline through a large LEFT-side window. A brass Hanukkah chanukiah sits clearly on that left window ledge, roughly x=8–30%, with the skyline and cold blue sky behind it. A warm shaded electric lamp and a small group of adult friends sharing conversation occupy the deeper RIGHT side of the room. Worn oak floor, soft upholstered chairs, small framed artwork with no text, and a navy throw create an intimate home. The broad foreground table is clear warm wood, not part of their side gathering.
Chanukiah accuracy: show ONE culturally accurate Hanukkah chanukiah, not a seven-branch menorah. Its simple brass candle holder has EXACTLY NINE visible candle positions: FOUR identical equal-height festival candles to the left, FOUR identical equal-height festival candles to the right, all EIGHT festival candles aligned in one straight horizontal row, plus ONE clearly raised central shamash/helper candle above the row. Every candle is individually visible and countable, with no overlapping, hidden or extra positions. Total candle count NINE. Keep this holder in the indicated side/background window or sideboard, never centered behind the future live beer glass.

Lighting count for first-night Hanukkah: exactly ONE festival candle is lit, the rightmost of the eight equal-height festival candles, and the single raised central shamash is also lit. EXACTLY TWO flames total. All seven other festival candles are visibly present but unlit, with dark bare wicks and no flame or halo.
Constraints: scenery only, adult friends or family, warm and specific Jewish Hanukkah gathering. NO foreground glass, bottle, beer, drink, cup, mug or can; no readable text, logos, signs, UI, border or watermark. NO Christmas tree, Santa, wreath, garland, stocking, cross, ornament, or generic Christmas blend. Do not introduce another candle holder or background candle flames that confuse the intended count. Keep all foreground table center empty. Maintain the opaque full-bleed portrait style.
